newsitem.title: CANADA: Williston Basin venture finds light sweet crude.
newsitem.headline: Williston Basin venture finds light sweet crude.

text.p: Silver Peak Resources Ltd said the Williston Basin Joint Venture's Navasota WJV Jan No.1 exploratory well in Richland County, Mont., tested 332 barrels daily of 47-degree gravity light sweet crude.
Silver Peak said the oil has already been contracted for sale at a premium of US $1.29 per barrel over the North Dakota reference price and first oil sales are expected to begin in one week.
The company said it has a 25 percent working interest in the Williston Basin Joint Venture, as does Golden Arch Resources. Navasota Resources Ltd owns 45 percent.

The well was completed in the Red River formation "C" zone from perforations between 12,330 and 12,337 feet and tested on a 13/64 inch choke flowing 99 percent clean oil accompanied by 149,000 cubic feet of natural gas per day.
Silver Peak said the well was shut in on August 3 for a 72-hour bottom hole pressure buildup test period. After this is finished, a production rate will be decided.

The well is the first of the Williston Basin Joint Venture's scheduled five well drilling program. More than 30 similar indicated seismic prospects have been identified on the Joint Venture's 39,899 gross mineral acres. The second well in the program will be announced shortly, the company said.
